checklist.notes: The manage sense of run, past-perfect sequencing, and consonant-to-vowel linking are appropriate development targets for internal tier B1.1; the prompts and expected responses remain within that level.

The set uses run naturally in the organize/manage sense. Exercise 002 now supplies the later past event “the meeting began,” so “had run” has a real past reference point rather than only a clock-time boundary.

The objective keys are defensible. In exercise 002, “Before the meeting began, Lan had run an event” uses every required word, expresses the intended earlier-before-later relationship, and is a natural English sentence; its listed variant is also natural.
This set contains no multiple-choice distractors. The constrained objective items instead provide explicit answer requirements and acceptable variants where relevant.

Instructions, stimuli, questions, answers, and rubric language are clear and natural overall. The explicit “run | an” boundary is intelligible task notation and does not make exercise 002’s primary sentence unnatural.

The set and audit declare project-authored text with no external payload or media. Manual local phrase-level inspection found no originality concern, but no Internet-wide or proprietary-corpus comparison was performed.
